Everything looks good. Here's a summary of what was done:

**The core trick**: Auth pages use `[ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]` to render as **static SSR**, where `HttpContext` is available. `App.razor` checks for this attribute and returns `null` (SSR) or `InteractiveServer` accordingly. All other pages stay globally interactive.

**Files created/modified:**

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Data/ApplicationDbContext.cs` | EF Identity context with in-memory DB |
| `Program.cs` | Added Identity services, EF InMemory, auth middleware, `AddCascadingAuthenticationState` |
| `Components/App.razor` | Conditional render mode via `RenderModeForPage` — SSR for auth pages, interactive for everything else |
| `Components/_Imports.razor` | Added `@using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization` |
| `Components/Layout/MainLayout.razor` | Auth-aware top bar: "Logged in as {email} \| Logout" or "Login \| Register" |
| `Components/Pages/Account/Login.razor` | SSR login form with `SignInManager.PasswordSignInAsync`, redirects to `/` |
| `Components/Pages/Account/Register.razor` | SSR register form with `UserManager.CreateAsync`, redirects to `/account/login` |
| `Components/Pages/Account/Logout.razor` | SSR page that calls `SignOutAsync` and redirects to `/` |
